q: How wide is a regulation ice hockey puck?
hint: For scale: a golf ball is about {4.3 cm} across.
card: Pucks are frozen before NHL games so they slide faster and bounce less on the ice.
clue: A tennis ball is about {6.7 cm} across.

q: What is a perfect score in a game of ten-pin bowling?
hint: For scale: a casual bowler often scores around 100 in a game.
card: A perfect game takes 12 strikes in a row: one in each of the first nine frames and three in the tenth.
clue: Top professional bowlers average around 220 a game.

q: How far apart are the bases on a Major League Baseball diamond?
hint: For scale: a bowling lane is about {18 m} from foul line to head pin.
card: The bases sit at the corners of a perfect square, with home plate at the fourth corner.
clue: A tennis court is about {24 m} long.

q: How far is the penalty spot from the goal line in soccer?
hint: For scale: a basketball rim is {3.05 m} off the floor.
card: Irish goalkeeper William McCrum came up with the penalty kick, and it was introduced in 1891.
clue: A full-size soccer goal is about {7.3 m} wide.

q: How long is the Kentucky Derby horse race?
hint: For scale: one lap of an outdoor running track is {0.4 km}.
card: It’s billed as “the most exciting two minutes in sports” because the winners finish in about two minutes.
clue: A mile is about {1.6 km}.

q: How tall is the FIFA World Cup trophy?
hint: For scale: a regulation basketball is about {24 cm} across.
card: It’s made of 18-karat gold, with two bands of green malachite around its base.
clue: A sheet of A4 paper is about {30 cm} long.

q: In what year was the first Boston Marathon run?
hint: For scale: the American Civil War ended in 1865.
card: It was inspired by the success of the first marathon at the modern Olympics, held the year before.
clue: Basketball was invented in 1891.

q: How many episodes of How I Met Your Mother were made?
hint: For scale: Breaking Bad ran for 62 episodes.
card: The Mother isn’t properly introduced until the season 8 finale.
clue: Seinfeld ran for 180 episodes.

q: How long is The Shawshank Redemption (1994), in minutes?
hint: For scale: Pixar’s Toy Story runs 81 minutes.
card: It struggled in theaters but went on to become the top rented film on home video.
clue: The Godfather runs 175 minutes.

q: In what year was Back to the Future released?
hint: For scale: Dr. No, the first James Bond film, came out in 1962.
card: Michael J. Fox shot it while still starring in the sitcom Family Ties, which took priority on his schedule.
clue: Jurassic Park came out in 1993.

q: How many Oscars did Bong Joon-ho’s Parasite (2019) win?
hint: For scale: Titanic won 11 Oscars.
card: It was the first film not in English to win Best Picture.
clue: The Silence of the Lambs won 5 Oscars.

q: In what year did Doctor Who first air on the BBC?
hint: For scale: the BBC began regular TV broadcasts in 1936.
card: The TARDIS is disguised as a police telephone box, a common sight on British streets when the show began.
clue: Elvis released “Heartbreak Hotel” in 1956.

q: In what year was DreamWorks’ first Shrek film released?
hint: For scale: Disney’s Aladdin came out in 1992.
card: It won the first-ever Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.
clue: Pixar’s Toy Story came out in 1995.

q: How many episodes of the original Star Trek series were made?
hint: For scale: Fawlty Towers made just 12 episodes.
card: Canceled after three seasons, it became an international hit in the 1970s through reruns on local stations.
clue: The Sopranos ran for 86 episodes.

q: In what year did Nirvana release the album Nevermind?
hint: For scale: the Beatles first played The Ed Sullivan Show in 1964.
card: In January 1992 it knocked Michael Jackson’s Dangerous off the top of the Billboard 200 album chart.
clue: Metallica’s Master of Puppets came out in 1986.

q: In what year was the first Glastonbury Festival held?
hint: For scale: Elvis released “Heartbreak Hotel” in 1956.
card: Tickets to the first one, then called the Pilton Festival, cost just £1.
clue: The Beatles first played The Ed Sullivan Show in 1964.

q: In what year did Fender introduce the Stratocaster electric guitar?
hint: For scale: Philips introduced the cassette tape in 1963.
card: Leo Fender designed it with a small team, and the company has made it without a break ever since.
clue: The first Grammy Awards were held in 1959.

q: In standard concert tuning, how many times per second does the A above middle C vibrate?
hint: For scale: the lowest note on a piano vibrates about 27 times per second.
card: The standard was agreed internationally in 1939; before that, orchestras in different cities tuned noticeably differently.
clue: Middle C vibrates about 262 times per second.

q: How many weeks did Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” spend at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100?
hint: For scale: Michael Jackson’s “Billie Jean” spent 7 weeks at No. 1.
card: Dolly Parton wrote the song and released it first, as a country single in 1974.
clue: “Despacito” spent 16 weeks at No. 1.

q: How many valves does a standard trumpet have?
hint: For scale: a standard guitar has six strings.
card: Its valves give eight possible combinations, but only seven different tube lengths.
clue: A standard violin has four strings.

q: How many lines make up a standard music staff?
hint: For scale: a standard piano has 88 keys.
card: Notes too high or low for the staff sit on short extra lines called ledger lines.
clue: A standard guitar has six strings.

q: How many squares make up each player’s ocean grid in classic Battleship?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 64 squares.
card: It was a pencil-and-paper game dating back to World War I, long before Milton Bradley’s 1967 board version.
clue: A Sudoku grid has 81 small squares.

q: In what year did YouTube launch?
hint: For scale: the World Wide Web became publicly available in 1991.
card: The first video ever uploaded, “Me at the zoo,” shows co-founder Jawed Karim at the San Diego Zoo.
clue: Google was founded in 1998.

q: In what year did LEGO patent its modern stud-and-tube brick?
hint: For scale: the Slinky first went on sale in 1945.
card: Bricks made today still snap firmly onto ones from the very first patented design.
clue: Mr. Potato Head went on sale in 1952.

q: How many little green houses come in a standard Monopoly set?
hint: For scale: a standard deck has 52 playing cards.
card: A standard set also comes with 12 hotels.
clue: A standard Monopoly set has 28 title deed cards.

q: In what year were Oreo cookies first sold?
hint: For scale: Coca-Cola was first sold in 1886.
card: It began as a knockoff of a cookie called Hydrox, which it went on to vastly outsell.
clue: Hershey’s milk chocolate bar debuted in 1900.

q: How many letter cubes come in a classic game of Boggle?
hint: For scale: a standard die has 6 faces.
card: Each round lasts three minutes, timed by a little sand timer.
clue: A chessboard is 8 squares wide.

q: How many squares are on a standard American bingo card, free space included?
hint: For scale: a tic-tac-toe grid has 9 squares.
card: The free space sits in the very center, so every line through the middle needs one fewer number.
clue: A standard deck has 52 playing cards.

q: How tall is London’s Gherkin skyscraper, 30 St Mary Axe?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty, ground to torch, is about {93 m} tall.
card: Despite all its curves, only one piece of glass in the building is curved: the lens-shaped cap at the very top.
clue: The Great Pyramid of Giza was about {147 m} tall when finished.

q: How tall is Taipei 101 in Taiwan?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
card: A giant steel ball weighing {660 t} hangs inside its upper floors to steady the tower in typhoons.
clue: The Empire State Building is about {443 m} to its antenna tip.

q: How tall is the seated statue of Abraham Lincoln in the Lincoln Memorial?
hint: For scale: a basketball rim is {3.05 m} off the floor.
card: If the seated Lincoln stood up, he would be about {8.5 m} tall.
clue: A London double-decker bus is about {4.4 m} tall.

q: In what year did the Burj Khalifa in Dubai open?
hint: For scale: the Channel Tunnel opened in 1994.
card: Its Y-shaped floor plan was inspired by the spider lily, a desert flower.
clue: Taipei 101 opened in 2004.

q: How tall was Kingda Ka in New Jersey, the world’s tallest roller coaster when it opened?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Riders were launched from zero to {206 km/h} in about 3.5 seconds.
clue: The Statue of Liberty, ground to torch, is about {93 m} tall.

q: How long is Venice’s Grand Canal?
hint: For scale: a marathon is about {42 km}.
card: Only four bridges cross it, the oldest being the Rialto Bridge.
clue: The Champs-Élysées in Paris is about {1.9 km} long.

q: In what year did New York’s Guggenheim Museum, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, open?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building opened in 1931.
card: It was Frank Lloyd Wright’s last major work; he died six months before it opened.
clue: The Sydney Opera House opened in 1973.

q: In what year did astronauts last walk on the Moon?
hint: For scale: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space in 1961.
card: Apollo 17 was the last crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit until Artemis II flew around the Moon in April 2026.
clue: Voyager 1 launched in 1977.

q: How much does the International Space Station weigh?
hint: For scale: a fully loaded semi truck weighs about {36 t}.
card: People have lived aboard it without a break since November 2000.
clue: A fully loaded Boeing 747-400 weighs about {400 t}.

q: What is the diameter of Jupiter, measured across its equator?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {12,742 km} across.
card: Jupiter is about two and a half times as massive as all the other planets combined.
clue: Saturn is about {116,460 km} across its equator.

q: In what year did NASA’s Viking 1 land on Mars?
hint: For scale: Sputnik 1 launched in 1957.
card: It was meant to land on July 4 for America’s bicentennial, but a rough landing site delayed it to July 20.
clue: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969.

q: How many minutes did Armstrong and Aldrin spend walking on the Moon during Apollo 11?
hint: For scale: a soccer match lasts 90 minutes.
card: They collected about {21.5 kg} of lunar samples to bring home.
clue: The Godfather runs 175 minutes.

q: How wide is the Hubble Space Telescope’s main mirror?
hint: For scale: the James Webb Space Telescope’s mirror is about {6.5 m} across.
card: Its mirror was ground slightly wrong, and astronauts fixed its blurry vision with corrective optics in 1993.
clue: A standard US interior door is about {2 m} tall.

q: What is the diameter of Venus?
hint: For scale: the Moon is about {3,475 km} across.
card: Venus spins in the opposite direction to most planets, a motion called retrograde rotation.
clue: Mars is about {6,779 km} across.

q: How many eyes does a box jellyfish have?
hint: For scale: most spiders have 8 eyes.
card: Some of its eyes have retinas, corneas and lenses, much like ours, even though it has no brain.
clue: A standard egg carton holds 12 eggs.

q: How many wings does a dragonfly have?
hint: For scale: a housefly gets by with just 2 wings.
card: Dragonflies can fly in six directions: up, down, forward, backward, left and right.
clue: Insects have 6 legs.

q: How long is a giraffe’s tongue?
hint: For scale: an adult human hand is about {19 cm} long.
card: It’s black, which may help protect it from sunburn while the giraffe feeds.
clue: A sheet of A4 paper is about {30 cm} long.

q: How much does an adult human liver weigh?
hint: For scale: a liter of water weighs {1 kg}.
card: The liver has a great capacity to regenerate, regrowing lost tissue after injury or surgery.
clue: An adult human brain weighs about {1.3 kg}.

q: In what year was a living coelacanth, a fish thought extinct with the dinosaurs, found?
hint: For scale: Charles Lindbergh flew solo across the Atlantic in 1927.
card: It turned up in a fisherman’s catch in South Africa and was spotted by museum curator Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer.
clue: Pluto was discovered in 1930.

q: In what year was insulin first used to treat a person with diabetes?
hint: For scale: the Titanic sank in 1912.
card: The first person treated with it was a boy in Toronto named Leonard Thompson.
clue: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928.

q: How many valves does the human heart have?
hint: For scale: humans have 2 lungs.
card: The “lub-dub” of a heartbeat is the sound of these valves closing.
clue: A human hand has 5 fingers.

q: How long was the original Route 66, from Chicago to Santa Monica?
hint: For scale: Paris to Berlin is about {880 km} as the crow flies.
card: John Steinbeck nicknamed it “the Mother Road” in The Grapes of Wrath.
clue: The Danube River is about {2,850 km} long.

q: About how many days did the Pony Express take to carry mail across its route?
hint: For scale: Nellie Bly went around the world in 72 days.
card: It ran for only about 18 months before the transcontinental telegraph made it obsolete.
clue: A week is 7 days.

q: For how many years did the Berlin Wall stand?
hint: For scale: World War II in Europe lasted about 6 years.
card: When it opened, souvenir hunters spent weeks chipping pieces off the Wall.
clue: The Cold War lasted about 45 years.

q: For how many years did Queen Elizabeth II reign?
hint: For scale: Henry VIII reigned for about 38 years.
card: She was the first British monarch to celebrate a Platinum Jubilee.
clue: Queen Victoria reigned for 63 years.

q: In what year did Lewis and Clark set off on their expedition west?
hint: For scale: the US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
card: Along the way they hired fur trapper Toussaint Charbonneau and his young Shoshone wife, Sacagawea.
clue: Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.

q: In what year did the Pilgrims hold the harvest feast often called the first Thanksgiving?
hint: For scale: Columbus first reached the Americas in 1492.
card: Having brought in a good harvest, the Pilgrims celebrated at Plymouth for three days that autumn.
clue: William Shakespeare died in 1616.

q: In what year did Abraham Lincoln deliver the Gettysburg Address?
hint: For scale: the US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
card: It has only 271 words, and Lincoln read it in less than two minutes.
clue: Gold was found at Sutter’s Mill in 1848.

q: What speed did the steam locomotive Mallard reach in 1938, the world record for steam?
hint: For scale: a cheetah can sprint at roughly {100 km/h}.
card: Mallard is now preserved at the National Railway Museum in York, England.
clue: A Formula 1 car can top {350 km/h}.

q: How long is the ocean liner Queen Mary 2?
hint: For scale: a soccer pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: When she was built in 2003, she was the longest passenger ship ever made.
clue: The Titanic was about {269 m} long.

q: How much did the original 1989 Nintendo Game Boy weigh, without batteries?
hint: For scale: a liter of water weighs {1 kg}.
card: It ran on four AA batteries, which lasted for roughly 30 hours of play.
clue: The original 2007 iPhone weighed about {0.135 kg}.

q: How much did the original 1984 Apple Macintosh weigh?
hint: For scale: a liter of water weighs {1 kg}.
card: It was introduced by the famous “1984” Super Bowl ad, directed by Ridley Scott.
clue: A US gallon of water weighs about {3.8 kg}.

q: In what year did the first Polaroid instant camera go on sale?
hint: For scale: the Ford Model T went on sale in 1908.
card: Edwin Land showed off his instant film in New York City a year before the first camera went on sale.
clue: The McDonald brothers opened their first restaurant in 1940.

q: In what year did Toyota launch the Prius, the first mass-produced hybrid car?
hint: For scale: the first iPhone came out in 2007.
card: The first-generation Prius was sold only in Japan.
clue: The World Wide Web became publicly available in 1991.

q: How heavy was the Wright brothers’ 1903 Flyer, without a pilot?
hint: For scale: a small car weighs about {1,000 kg}.
card: Its first flight covered about {37 m}, less than the wingspan of a modern jumbo jet.
clue: A full-grown male lion weighs about {190 kg}.

q: How many stripes are on the flag of the United States?
hint: For scale: the flag has 50 stars.
card: The stripes stand for the thirteen British colonies that won independence.
clue: A rugby union team has 15 players on the field.

q: How many US states have a coastline on the Pacific Ocean?
hint: For scale: the United States has fifty states.
card: Hawaii and Alaska both count, and Alaska alone has more coastline than all the other states combined.
clue: Four US states border Mexico.

q: How many provinces does Canada have?
hint: For scale: there are 50 US states.
card: Its newest province, Newfoundland and Labrador, joined in 1949.
clue: Australia has six states.

q: What is the area of Greenland?
hint: For scale: Texas covers about {696,000 sq km}.
card: About 81% of it is covered by an ice sheet.
clue: Argentina covers about {2,780,000 sq km}.

q: How tall is Mount Fuji in Japan?
hint: For scale: Mount Everest is about {8,849 m} tall.
card: Its last eruption ran from 1707 to 1708, and its near-perfect cone is a dormant volcano.
clue: The Matterhorn is about {4,478 m} tall.

q: How tall is Horseshoe Falls, the biggest of the three Niagara Falls?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: In 1901, a 63-year-old schoolteacher, Annie Edson Taylor, became the first person to go over the falls in a barrel, and survived.
clue: The Arc de Triomphe in Paris is about {50 m} tall.

q: How many sides does a standard stop sign have?
hint: For scale: a yield sign has 3 sides.
card: Its unique shape lets drivers facing the back of the sign know that oncoming traffic has to stop.
clue: A hexagon has 6 sides.
